'''Vít Krejčí''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|v|i:|t|_|ˌ|k|r|eɪ|ˈ|ʧ|i:}}; born 19 June 2000) is a Czech professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was drafted in the second round of the [[2020 NBA draft]].

==Early life and career==
Krejčí was born in [[Strakonice]], Czech Republic and played basketball for the youth academy of Sokol Pisek.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vít Krejci: así lo ha hecho el base que empieza a despuntar en el Casademont Zaragoza |url=https://www.gigantes.com/liga-endesa/jovenes-promesas/vit-krejci-asi-lo-ha-hecho-el-base-que-empieza-a-despuntar-en-el-casademont-zaragoza-video/ |publisher=Gigantes del Basket |access-date=27 June 2020 |language=es |date=21 May 2020}}</ref> At age 14, he joined [[Spanish basketball clubs in international competitions|Spanish basketball club]], [[Basket Zaragoza|Zaragoza]]. In the 2016–17 season, he began playing for Anagan Olivar, the [[reserve team]] of Zaragoza, in the [[Liga EBA]].<ref name="hein">{{cite web |last=Hein |first=David |title=Krejci growing in confidence with Zaragoza and Czechs |url=http://www.championsleague.basketball/19-20/news/krejci-growing-in-confidence-with-zaragoza-and-czechs |publisher=[[Basketball Champions League]] |access-date=27 June 2020 |date=26 March 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Basket Zaragoza (2017–2021)===
On 5 March 2017, at 16 years and eight months of age, Krejčí made his professional debut for Zaragoza against [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]]. He tied with [[Sergi García (basketball)|Sergi García]] as the second-youngest debutant in club history, behind [[Carlos Alocén]].<ref name=hein/> On 17 April 2020, Krejčí declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Vit Krejci: Declares for draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/vit-krejci-declares-for-draft/ |work=CBS Sports |access-date=27 June 2020 |date=17 April 2020}}</ref> In the 2019–20 season, Krejčí averaged 3.2 points in 9.2 minutes per game and was named to the [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB All-Young Players Team]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mejor Quinteto Joven El Corte Inglés de la Liga Endesa 2019-20 |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/153499-mejor-quinteto-joven-el-corte-ingles-de-la-liga-endesa-201920.html |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |access-date=27 June 2020 |language=es |date=25 June 2020}}</ref> On 25 September 2020, he suffered a season-ending left knee injury in a game against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Askounis |first=Johnny |title=Knee injury sidelines Vit Krejci for the remainder of the season |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1106090/knee-injury-sidelines-vit-krejci-for-the-remainder-of-the-season/|publisher=EuroHoops|access-date=27 September 2020|date=27 September 2020}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021–2022)===
Krejčí was selected with the 37th overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2020 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Albert|last=Lee|title=2020 NBA Draft: Wizards select Vit Krejci No. 37 overall, then trade him to the Thunder for the No. 53 pick|url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/2020/11/18/21574135/2020-nba-draft-washington-wizards-vit-krejci-no-37-overall|website=BulletsForever.com|date=18 November 2020|access-date=8 December 2020}}</ref> and subsequently traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Admiral Schofield and Draft Rights to Vít Krejčí|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/schofield-krejci-201119|website=NBA.com|date=19 November 2020|access-date=8 December 2020}}</ref> On 28 January 2021, he signed with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]], the Thunder's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, where he rehabbed the ACL injury he sustained in Zaragoza.<ref>{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces 2020-21 Roster|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-2020-21-roster/|website=NBA G League|date=28 January 2021|access-date=15 February 2021}}</ref>

On 2 September 2021, Krejčí signed a multi-year deal with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mussatto |first=Joe |date=3 September 2021 |title=Vit Krejci signs multi-year contract with OKC Thunder |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2021/09/03/vit-krejci-signs-contract-okc-thunder/5712961001 |access-date=10 September 2023 |website=oklahoman.com}}</ref>

=== Atlanta Hawks (2022–2023) ===
On 27 September 2022, Krejčí was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Maurice Harkless]] and draft considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Acquire Vit Krejci|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-vit-krejci|website=NBA.com|date=27 September 2022|access-date=2 October 2022}}</ref>

On 16 August 2023, Krejčí was waived by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Vit Krejci|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-on-vit-krejci|website=NBA.com|date=16 August 2023|access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref>

===Iowa Wolves (2023)===
On 14 September 2023, Krejčí signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Vít Krejčí|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-vit-krejci|website=NBA.com|date=14 September 2023|access-date=14 September 2023}}</ref> but was waived on 19 October.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign D.J. Carton|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-d-j-carton|website=NBA.com|date=19 October 2023|access-date=20 October 2023}}</ref> Ten days later, he joined the [[Iowa Wolves]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=29 October 2023|access-date=8 December 2023}}</ref>

===Second stint with Hawks (2023–2026)===
On 22 December 2023, Krejčí signed another two-way contract with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Forward Vit Krejci to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-forward-vit-krejci-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=22 December 2023|access-date=25 December 2023}}</ref> He made 22 appearances (14 starts) for Atlanta during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 6.1 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vit Krejci 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4578893/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=January 8, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 12 July 2024, Krejčí signed a four-year, $10 million contract extension with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Forward Vít Krejčí|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-forward-vit-krejci|website=NBA.com|date=12 July 2024|access-date=13 July 2024}}</ref> He played in 57 games (including 16 starts) for the Hawks during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.2 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 2.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vit Krejci 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4578893/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=January 8, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 10 November 2025, Krejčí scored a career-high 28 points, including a career-high eight three pointers on ten attempts, as Atlanta defeated the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]] 105–102.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Krejci scores career-high 28 points as Hawks send Clippers to fifth straight loss, 105-102|url=https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2025/11/11/krejci-scores-career-high-28-points-hawks-send-clippers-fifth-straight-loss-105-102/|access-date=January 8, 2026|website=atlantanewsfirst.com|language=en}}</ref> He made 46 total appearances for the Hawks during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], compiling averages of 9.0 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vit Krejci 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4578893/vit-krejci|access-date=April 13, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2026–present)===
On 1 February 2026, Krejčí was traded to the Portland Trail Blazers in exchange for [[Duop Reath]], a 2027 second round pick, and a 2030 second round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers Aquire [sic] Vit Krejci|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-aquire-vit-krejci|access-date=February 4, 2026|website=trailblazers.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Krejčí represented the Czech Republic on several occasions at the youth level. He was named to the All-Star Five of the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship Division B]] in [[Matosinhos]], Portugal after averaging 14.9 points, 5.1 rebounds and 5.1 assists, leading his team to the silver medal. In February 2019, Krejčí made his debut for the [[Czech Republic men's national basketball team|senior national team]] during the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification]] stage.<ref name=hein/>
